parameters.note: Heather Lake is a high-alpine lake (~7,900 ft) in the Desolation Wilderness (El Dorado Co.), on the Glen Alpine chain between Susie Lake and Lake Aloha. (There are several other Heather Lakes in California — in Fresno, Tulare, and Siskiyou cos. — so this file is the El Dorado / Desolation Wilderness one.) It sits within the Lake Tahoe basin but well upstream of the 'first lake': its outlet drains east to Susie Lake and Glen Alpine Creek, which feeds Fallen Leaf Lake and then Taylor Creek into Lake Tahoe; going up Taylor Creek the first lake reached is Fallen Leaf Lake, far below Heather. The special Lake Tahoe tributary closure (§7.50(b)(152), which reaches only flowing tributaries upstream to the first lake) therefore does not apply to this lake. It is not listed by name in §7.40(b) or §7.50(b), so the general statewide lake regulation §5.85(a)(1) governs: open all year, 5/10. It is not in CDFW's 2026 provisional stocking plan; brook, brown, and rainbow trout ('Brookies and Browns up to 17", some Rainbows') are reported by a third-party angling reference (flyfishingthesierra.com).

candidates.summary: Open all year (general statewide lake regulation; not listed as a special-regulation water)
